cores.culture: Evidence supports culture-related differences in object-versus-context allocation, but effects can vary by task and sample.
cores.gap: Need more globally diverse and social-media-specific transport evidence.

cores.culture: Specific curiosity instruments show cross-cultural portability in Germany/UK and an Indonesian adaptation, but not universal invariance.
cores.gap: Need broader non-WEIRD state-curiosity and information-avoidance evidence.

cores.culture: Emotion experience, ideal arousal and emotion measurement show cultural variation; method effects can inflate observed differences.
cores.gap: Need direct cultural transport evidence for social-media valuation/appraisal processes.

cores.culture: Identity constructs and measurement are culturally sensitive; cross-national measurement invariance is incomplete for some collective/interdependent components.
cores.gap: Need platform-specific identity salience and identity-switching evidence.

cores.culture: Credibility/trust effects vary by geographical and methodological context; participant type also moderates heuristic-cue effects.
cores.gap: Need validated cross-cultural source/message trust measurement invariance in social-media contexts.

cores.culture: Parasocial associations differ by cultural region and age; construct type (PSI versus PSR) materially changes pooled associations.
cores.gap: Need longitudinal causal evidence across cultures, not only association.

cores.culture: Cross-cultural reviews indicate self-construal and cultural background can shape social-media communication/sharing, while audience and platform factors also matter.
cores.gap: Need stronger cross-cultural behavioral sharing datasets with common measurement.

cores.culture: No strong cross-cultural measurement-invariance evidence was found in this cycle; culture remains an explicit transport uncertainty.
